_comment: B2-AC29. A fresh in-repo audit of every DOM/CSS/browser-only construct on the shared path, re-run during this ticket's implementation (not inherited from the TaskSpec's quoted count). Each entry is file:line -> construct -> named native substitute -> disposition, classified against the ACTUAL built native bundle (dist/index.native.js) and the pinned react-native/@tamagui typings, not asserted. 'lines' is a parallel array, one number per comma-separated path in 'file', in the SAME order — added this pass (review finding) after `check-native-audit.mjs` grew a line-sanity check. For an entry whose construct has already been extracted out to a named seam (the normal, successful outcome of this ticket's work), the line points at the CURRENT consumption/import site of that seam in the named file, not at a now-removed literal — the construct text itself documents what USED to be there and where it moved to; it is not a promise that grepping for the construct's exact substring at that line will still succeed post-refactor. 'disposition' is one of: handled-by-tamagui (Tamagui's own native prop/style resolution already does the right thing — no seam needed), silently-dropped (Tamagui silently ignores the construct on native — no warning, but also no behaviour, so a seam supplies the real native equivalent when one matters), invalid-needs-seam (would be wrong or crash on native without a seam), visually-wrong-needs-seam (renders something, but not the intended thing, without a seam). Several entries below correct assumptions made before this file existed — see the 'measured' note on each.

entries.substitute: src/internal/useCapOffset.native.ts (fixed pre-measurement value, B2-AC13)
src/internal/useScrollEdges.native.ts (onLayout/onScroll/onContentSizeChange via Scroll.native.tsx)

entries.construct: scrollIntoView on a ref cast to HTMLElement
entries.substitute: src/internal/Scroll.tsx/.native.tsx's ScrollHandle.scrollChildIntoView
src/internal/Scroll.tsx/.native.tsx's ScrollHandle.scrollByPage
src/internal/tileDepth.native.ts (shadowColor/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius/elevationAndroid)
src/internal/tileDepth.native.ts (RGB-channel darken() approximation; recorded as an allowed rendering difference, not pixel-identical)

entries.construct: --bobuttons-tile-shadow custom property, consumed by BobuttonsProvider's injected CSS rule
entries.substitute: src/internal/tileDepth.ts/.native.ts resolve to platform-appropriate style props directly; the custom property is web-only
src/provider/BobuttonsProvider.native.tsx (drops the element entirely; each rule's job is done at its own seam instead)
src/provider/BobuttonsProvider.native.tsx (flex: 1 — minHeight:"100%" resolves against an unsized parent on native)
src/internal/platformStyles.ts/.native.ts's FILL_VIEWPORT (flex: 1)

entries.construct: display: "inline-flex" (6 sites: Button's ButtonFrame, Checkbox's Check, TextInput's Frame, Icon's IconFrame, IconButton's Frame, SquareGrid's Content)
entries.substitute: src/internal/platformStyles.native.ts's INLINE_FLEX (alignSelf: "flex-start") — MEASURED CORRECTION: RN's display is 'none'|'flex'|'contents' and its default is already 'flex', so the previously-assumed substitute display:"flex" would have stretched all six to their parent's full width with every gate green.

src/internal/platformStyles.native.ts's DISABLED_CURSOR ({}) — the only cursor site needing a seam; every other cursor value in the tree ("pointer"/"auto") is inside RN's CursorValue and stays on the shared path.

entries.construct: whiteSpace: "nowrap" / textOverflow: "ellipsis" inside a styled(Text, {...}) base style (ListRow's Detail, AppHeader's Title and DateLabel, Tabs' TabLabel)
entries.substitute: src/internal/singleLineText.ts/.native.ts's SINGLE_LINE ({ numberOfLines: 1 }) — MEASURED CORRECTION: @tamagui/helpers's nonAnimatableWebTextProps lists whiteSpace/textOverflow/wordWrap as web-only keys Tamagui's native style pipeline SKIPS, not converts to numberOfLines/ellipsizeMode as this ticket originally assumed. Tamagui's native Text host does default ellipsizeMode to "tail" on its own, so numberOfLines alone is enough.

none — MEASURED: react-native's FlexAlignType includes 'baseline' (StyleSheetTypes.d.ts), so Yoga implements it on native. No longer a seam; any remaining Yoga-vs-browser text-baseline difference is a B2-AC16 parity item, recorded in the README.

entries.construct: tabIndex (TabBar's TabButton, ListRow's select control — both styled(View, ...) Tamagui components)
entries.substitute: none — MEASURED: Tamagui maps tabIndex to React Native's `focusable` prop (viewProps.focusable = Number(tabIndex) >= 0) directly on its own native style/prop pipeline, so it is an ACTIVE mapped prop, not inert.

entries.construct: tabIndex passed to the Scroll seam (ViewBody, SettingsLayout) and role/aria-label/aria-orientation passed to Scroll for the mobile tab list (TabBar)
entries.substitute: src/internal/Scroll.native.tsx — CORRECTED THIS PASS (review finding): a bare RN `ScrollView` is not a Tamagui component, so Tamagui's tabIndex->focusable mapping does not apply to it; Scroll.native.tsx now forwards tabIndex->focusable, role and aria-label itself, directly on the ScrollView. `aria-orientation` has no RN equivalent (ViewAccessibility.d.ts carries no such prop) and stays inert, named in the README's B2-AC5(c) list.

src/internal/platformStyles.ts/.native.ts's dataAttrs() — MEASURED: Tamagui silently drops unrecognised data-* props on native (no warning), so this is bundle hygiene and a B2-AC12 scan token, not a B2-AC2 defect risk.

entries.construct: hidden <input type="checkbox"> for native keyboard/screen-reader behaviour
entries.substitute: src/internal/TextField.tsx/.native.tsx (kind="checkbox" — a Pressable with accessibilityRole="checkbox" on native)
src/internal/CheckGlyph.tsx/.native.tsx (two rotated Views on native — no react-native-svg peer; griddy-icons cannot render on native under any peer anyway, B2-AC18)
src/internal/CloseGlyph.native.tsx (fixed-pixel two-View glyph; em units do not exist on native)

entries.construct: bare <input> + BARE_INPUT CSSProperties bag (flex/width/`color: inherit`/`font: inherit`, plus the `[data-bobuttons-input]::placeholder` rule for the placeholder colour)
entries.substitute: src/internal/TextField.tsx/.native.tsx (kind="text" — RN TextInput on native, with the B2-AC5(d) keyboard/autoCorrect/autoCapitalize/secureTextEntry mapping). CORRECTED THIS PASS (review finding): RN does not inherit a parent Text's colour/font/size into a child TextInput the way a DOM <input> inherits `color: inherit`/`font: inherit`, so the native half explicitly resolves `$color`/`$textFaint`/body font via useCssColor/fontFamilies.native rather than relying on inheritance; `placeholderTextColor` replaces the `::placeholder` rule. TextInput's `mono` variant stays web/Frame-only (not threaded through this seam, to avoid moving web bundle bytes for a native-only font-family choice) — named as an accepted divergence in the README's B2-AC5(c) list.
src/internal/TessellatedPattern.tsx/.native.tsx (explicit tile replication over a measured area on native, B2-AC13 first-frame: no pattern until the first onLayout)

entries.construct: linear-gradient(...) CSS string built from theme.*.variable reads (AppHeader title, ViewPane/SettingsSection stripes, TabBar's two edge fades)
entries.substitute: src/internal/useAccentGradient.native.ts — D4 (decided at plan approval): flat-colour fallback everywhere (flat $primary text colour, solid $accent stripe, flat background-coloured fade strip), not RN 0.79's experimental_backgroundImage and not a react-native-linear-gradient/masked-view peer. Recorded in the README's divergence list.
src/internal/cssColor.native.ts (theme[name]?.val, a concrete value; throws loudly if unresolved — B2-AC12's "fails loudly rather than rendering nothing")
src/tokens/fontFamilies.ts/.native.ts (single system face name per platform — RN's fontFamily takes one name, not a CSS stack; B2-AC17)

entries.construct: Intl.DateTimeFormat/Intl.NumberFormat with a locale and timeZone that may not be ICU-available on Hermes
entries.substitute: src/internal/formatInstant.native.ts (try/catch fallback to a locale-free format, never throws at render; B2-AC26)

entries.construct: onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave-only hover, and Button.tsx's bespoke onMouseEnter/Leave/Down/Up interaction state machine
entries.substitute: src/internal/interaction.native.ts's useInteractive/useHover (hovered permanently false, B2-AC5(a); pressed from onPressIn/onPressOut; activationKeyHandlers returns {}, B2-AC5(b))

entries.construct: color="currentColor" passed into the consumer-supplied IconSource (no native equivalent of the CSS currentColor keyword)
entries.substitute: none — resolve the same colour explicitly via useCssColor()'s toCss(ink), the identical pattern Icon.tsx already uses for its own Source (toCss(token)); on native toCss resolves to a concrete value instead of a CSS keyword.

entries.construct: flexGrow/flexBasis passed through to the scroll container (TabBar's mobile HORIZONTAL_FRAME: flexGrow={0} flexBasis="auto", to stop the tab strip stretching to fill its Frame)
entries.substitute: src/internal/Scroll.native.tsx — CORRECTED THIS PASS (review finding): the native half previously declared these props on ScrollProps but never read them, hardcoding style={{flex:1}} regardless, so TabBar's mobile tab strip always stretched full-width on native. Now forwarded into the ScrollView's own style (flexGrow ?? 1 / flexShrink: 1 / flexBasis ?? 0) when either is supplied. Yoga caveat recorded for future seams: resolveFlexBasis returns points(0) for flexBasis:"auto" ONLY when the resolved flex is > 0 — TabBar's flexGrow={0} case does not hit that, so "auto" resolves to content-based sizing as intended.

entries.construct: useMedia() breakpoint read (no document/window access) — named in B2-AC13 as requiring either a native implementation or a documented justification for needing none
entries.substitute: none needed — handled-by-tamagui: the hook is 9 lines of useMedia() with zero DOM access, and @tamagui/core's native build backs useMedia() with its own NativeMediaQueryList (Dimensions-driven, see B2-AC28). No .native.ts sibling exists; this entry is the required justification record.

_accessibilityAuditComment: B2-AC20. Per-export enumeration of every role/aria-*/tabIndex prop against React Native's supported accessibility surface (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Components/View/ViewAccessibility.d.ts, measured this pass), one entry per public export (25 components + BobuttonsProvider = 26). 'disposition' is one of: rn-native (the exact prop name — role value included — exists in RN's Role/AccessibilityProps types and is forwarded verbatim by Tamagui's native prop pipeline, which passes any unrecognised non-style key through to the host component's props as-is), mapped (tabIndex -> RN's `focusable`, either by Tamagui's own native style pipeline on a styled(View/Text,...) component, or by Scroll.native.tsx forwarding it directly — see the tabIndex entries above), inert-no-rn-equivalent (the prop has NO RN counterpart at all — not even an unmapped pass-through target — so it reaches the host component as an unrecognised prop; MEASURED that RN's own `role`/aria-* types list has no `aria-level`/`aria-pressed`/`aria-controls`/`aria-orientation`, and that Tamagui's native getSplitStyles.native.js has no special case for them, so they fall through to its default `viewProps[key] = value` assignment — whether an unrecognised prop on a host View/Text causes a console warning is NOT verified by any committed script per the approved scope change (no device harness committed), so each inert-no-rn-equivalent prop is also a named item for the owner's manual on-device B2-AC2 check), none (no accessibility props on this export at all).

accessibilityAudit.notes: role/aria-label/aria-disabled are rn-native; tabIndex is mapped via Tamagui's own native pipeline (ButtonFrame is a styled(View,...)).
All three are in RN's supported prop set.
role values are rn-native; aria-level has no RN equivalent (no concept of heading depth) — manual check: confirm no console warning.
